intro: Chon Buri is more than beaches and Pattaya nightlife. Its 2026 Michelin list runs to five Bib Gourmand spots, from the wood-smoke sticky rice at Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao to the generous Thai spreads at Pladids. It is barely an hour from Bangkok, so you can eat a Michelin lunch without booking weeks ahead.
quickAnswerHtml: Chon Buri has 5 Michelin 2026 restaurants, all Bib Gourmand (no starred spots yet).

Its 2026 Michelin list runs to five Bib Gourmand spots, from the wood-smoke sticky rice at Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao to the generous Thai spreads at Pladids. It is barely an hour from Bangkok, so you can eat a Michelin lunch without booking weeks ahead.

blocks.name: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao is at 357 Sukhumvit Road, Saen Suk sub-district, Nong Mon area, Chon Buri, right across from the PTT petrol station in Nong Mon. Driving from Bangkok via the motorway toward Bang Saen, you'll pass right by the shop. It's open roughly 08:00-17:00 or until sold out, and closed every Wednesday — don't forget to check the day before you go. This is a takeaway-only shop with no seating, cash only, no advance booking needed, but if you want to order a large quantity or check whether stock remains, call 086-512-8498 or 081-453-0405

Sold by the tube, a budget under THB 200 per person gets you several tubes to take home. Both white and black sticky rice are available, in long and short tubes. Taro and black bean fillings are available every day, while custard filling is made only on Saturdays and Sundays. The best time to go is in the morning, since the shop grills khao lam fresh daily over charcoal and it sells out fast, especially on holidays when plenty of people stop by on their way to Bang Saen. Arrive in the late afternoon and you risk coming away empty-handed. Pair the trip with Bang Saen beach, just a few minutes further down the road Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Fresh coconut milk khao lam grilled over charcoal, fragrant with bamboo, filled with taro, black bean, and custard
mustOrder: White/black sticky rice khao lam (long and short tubes)
blocks.bestFor: Stop for a souvenir on the way to Bang Saen, an old-school dessert favourite, for those chasing Bib Gourmand finds on a light budget
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao official Facebook page

blocks.name: Krua Laew Tae R-Rom
blocks.descHtml:
Budget around 200–500 THB per person. The restaurant is open roughly 11:30–20:00, closed Wednesdays, but the key rule here is "whatever the ingredients allow" — on a day when the seafood catch doesn't cooperate, the restaurant may close or lose half its menu, so always call ahead before leaving your hotel. Call 090-987-1101 or message the restaurant's Facebook page — there's no online booking system. During peak periods like long weekends, book about a week ahead, since the restaurant is small with limited seating.

The restaurant sits on Soi Phaniat Chang in Na Kluea, North Pattaya, a short drive north from central Pattaya, close to the fishing community and Na Kluea fish market. If you haven't booked, arrive around 10 minutes before opening to catch the first seating, since standout dishes like the triggerfish red curry or Thai fish sashimi are limited to whatever's fresh that day — arrive late and you may just hear "sold out." Weekday afternoons are noticeably quieter than weekends. This suits diners who plan ahead and can stay flexible about what's on the menu. Read the full review →
mustOrder: Squid stir-fried in its own ink
blocks.bestFor: Genuine fresh-seafood fans who want to taste the cooking of a Na Kluea home kitchen, don't need a fixed menu, and love a small restaurant worth planning ahead for

blocks.name: La Voi (La Voi Pattaya)
blocks.descHtml:
La Voi is on Chaiyaphruek Road, on the side heading toward Jomtien Beach — easy to spot near Seven Condo, in Pattaya's Jomtien–Nong Prue area. The restaurant is open Tuesday–Friday 09:00–18:00, Saturday–Sunday 09:00–16:30, and closed every Monday — remember the closing day, since plenty of people miss it. It's walk-in only, with no table booking system; if you want to check ahead whether it's open or whether dishes have sold out, call 097-161-5566.

On budget: noodles and gao lao run about THB 70–120 a bowl, La Voi rice is THB 150, and the bai phai hot pot for sharing across the table is THB 385. On average, budget around THB 150–300 per person for a full meal. The restaurant is halal, so Muslim friends can eat here without worry, and the dress code is casual — no need to overthink it. The best time to go is lunch, since the restaurant closes fairly early (6pm on weekdays, 4:30pm on weekends) — don't plan on dinner here. Anyone driving from central Pattaya or Jomtien Beach is only a few minutes away, making it a perfect stop before or after a swim at Jomtien. Read the full review →
blocks.bestFor: Genuine beef-noodle fans, a great-value lunch near Jomtien, and Muslim travelers looking for MICHELIN-level halal food in Pattaya
blocks.libCredit: Photo: La Voi Pattaya official Facebook page

blocks.name: Lung Shall Kitchen
blocks.descHtml:
Lung Shall Kitchen is walk-in only — no advance bookings — but you can call ahead with questions at 086-089-1692. It's easy on the wallet: about 100–200 THB a dish, averaging 250–400 THB a head for a full seafood-and-som-tam spread. The restaurant is open roughly 10:00–20:00, though MICHELIN notes an afternoon break from 14:00–17:30, so for a sure visit come for lunch before 2pm or dinner after 5:30pm. Keep this in mind: the restaurant is closed on the 13th and 26th of every month — miss those two dates and you'll have made the trip for nothing.

The restaurant sits on Nong Mai Kaen Road, in the Noen Plub Wan, Nong Prue area on the East Pattaya side, just before the Noen Plub Wan Ua-Athon village. Your own car is the easiest way in, since it's outside the tourist walking zone. Everything is cooked fresh to order, so expect some wait — order everything up front, then settle in and enjoy the breeze in the open-air wooden dining room while the food comes out. Dress is casual. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Noen Plub Wan, Nong Prue (East Pattaya)
blocks.signature: Deep-fried triggerfish in fish sauce, fried so crisp you can eat the bones
mustOrder: Squid stir-fried in black ink sauce
Young coconut shoot and fresh shrimp som tam
blocks.bestFor: Road-trippers chasing the MICHELIN trail who want local-price home-style seafood away from the Pattaya tourist zone
blocks.zone: Noen Plub Wan, Nong Prue (East Pattaya)

blocks.name: Pladids
blocks.descHtml:
Pladids takes bookings in advance only — no walk-ins, ever. It's open for two dinner sittings only: 17:00–18:30 and 19:00–20:30, seating roughly 2 tables per sitting per day. To book, follow the restaurant's Facebook page (facebook.com/pladids.mp), which announces booking windows periodically, or call 084-455-6145 — the queue fills up fast, and most people need to book a month or more ahead. If you're planning a Pattaya trip, book this before you even book your hotel. The seasonal set runs around THB 500–1,000 per person (Wongnai lists it as THB 501–1,000), and the dress code is casual.

The restaurant is in Tambon Pong, Bang Lamung, on the east Pattaya side, a fair distance from the beach zone and the walking street, with no public transport passing by — you'll need to drive or grab a ride. It's worth pinning the exact coordinates from the restaurant's page before you set off, allowing about 20–30 minutes from central Pattaya, and aim to arrive 10–15 minutes before your sitting, since each sitting runs exactly an hour and a half. There's no menu to choose from — the chef builds the set from whatever the small fishing boats bring in that day, so flag any seafood allergies when you book. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: A seasonal seafood set sourced from small fishing boats, served with jasmine rice
mustOrder: The seasonal seafood set (no fixed menu — the chef builds it from what the boats bring in that day)
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants real eastern-seaboard seafood straight from small fishing boats, chef's-table style, up close — great for couples or small groups who can plan a month ahead

faq.q: How many Michelin restaurants are in Chon Buri?
faq.a: Five in 2026, all Bib Gourmand: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao, Krua Laew Tae R-ROM, La Voi, Lung Shall Kitchen and Pladids. There are no starred restaurants yet.

faq.q: Which one should I book ahead?
faq.a: Pladids is the priciest on the list at roughly 500–1,000 baht per person and serves full sit-down Thai spreads, so it is worth calling ahead, especially on weekends.

faq.q: Where should I go for a cheap, light bite?
faq.a: La Voi in Pattaya is the most wallet-friendly at around 70–120 baht, perfect for a small meal. Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao is also easy to grab and go for about 200 baht.

faq.q: Are these restaurants in the city or near Pattaya?
faq.a: They are split across both. La Voi sits on the Pattaya side, while Krua Laew Tae R-ROM, Lung Shall Kitchen and Pladids are in and around Chon Buri town, so check the map and plan your route first.

faq.q: How many can I eat at in one day?
faq.a: With only five spots relatively close together, a well-planned day of driving lets you hit two or three. Start light at La Voi, then finish with a full Thai dinner at Pladids.
